articles.title: “A community to lean on”: LeBron James’ foundation welcomes Akron children back to school as NBA icon continues supporting his hometown
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, and his wife Savannah James have remained committed to their hometown, Akron, even as they are
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, and his wife Savannah James have remained committed to their hometown, Akron, even as they are constantly surrounded by their fame and busy lives. As LeBron James gears up to get back to the court in the next few weeks, his foundation’s education wing, the I PROMISE School,has shared a new update about the new school year.LeBron James’ foundation makes a new update about children starting the new school year as the NBA icon stands by Akron’s childrenA few hours ago, LeBron James' I PROMISE School took to its social media to make a post about their students.The post read as, “Welcome Home, 3rd grade! Sorting Day is a moment our 3rd graders won’t forget. One by one, our scholars stepped up to the House Wheel to find out where they’d land, joining a House full of new connections, traditions, support and, of course, their people. 💚”The post also added, “What starts with a spin becomes a sense of belonging, a community to lean on and a whole new way to experience what it means to be part of IPS. 😁🥳 5 Houses. 1 IPS. One family.”Set up in 2018, LeBron James’ foundation, the LeBron James Family Foundation’s education wing, has remained committed to being there for students in Akron.LeBron James reflects on growing up in Akron and the difficult days he has had to manage with his mother raising himA lot of it has been inspired by the childhood LeBron James has had in Akron before he made it big in the league after being drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers.A few years ago, in an interview with Teen Vogue, the 41 year old NBA star player reflected on his childhood as he said, “I think the best way that I managed those struggles growing up as a kid was just always understanding that there’s loved ones around me that want me to succeed and there’s loved ones around me that want me to be great.”LeBron James said, “Even though the adults and the people that we love are going through so much, they don’t want us to feel that burden. They want us to continue to be as positive as possible because they see the bright future in us. Even though there were some days I felt like it wasn’t the best day for me personally, or for my mom, I always felt like there would be brighter days.”For now, there are rumors about LeBron James retiring after his new season with the Philadelphia 76ers. articles.title: “I was very nervous”: LeBron James’ wife Savannah James opens up on finding her voice after years away from the spotlight
articles.summary: LeBron James, the 41 year old NBA icon, might be the greatest player in the world but he has always been a family fan first.
articles.body: LeBron James, the 41 year old NBA icon, might be the greatest player in the world but he has always been a family fan first. The NBA legend has fondly spoken of his wife and the mother of his three children, Savannah James, ever since he joined the league. While Savannah James preferred to stay out of the spotlight for a long time, she has now turned into a successful podcaster and an entrepreneur. Ahead of the new season, Savannah James has spoken about how nervous she was before she went public.LeBron James’ wife Savannah James reflects on how people perceived her for staying out of the spotlight and the judgement she expectedA few months ago, in an interview with NBC, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James reflected on her decisions as she said, "The way I was perceived was very quiet, very 'She doesn't talk,' very 'Does she talk?' like I don't have a voice…”LeBron James’ wife Savannah James added, “So while I was very nervous, I was also looking forward to sharing a part of myself that a lot of people hadn't seen before."The founder of Reframe Beauty continued, "I felt like this is something fun that I want to do with my friend," says James. "We thought it would be a great idea to take these calls and give [our] perspective."LeBron James’ wife Savannah James also reflected on the judgement she had expected as she said, "I don't care how I'm being judged because this is who I am," says James. "While that came with a little bit of nervousness, it also came with a lot of liberation."She added, "It was all about me. It was really liberating and really exciting," she says. "While first it came with nerves, it ended up being really, really special."LeBron James’ wife Savannah James works on multiple successful ventures as she stands by her husband’s sideFor the unversed, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James has been working on her popular podcast, Everybody’s Crazy, alongside her close friend April McDaniel, for the last few years.While Savannah James and her co-host and friend, April McDaniel mostly discuss their bond, their lives and marriages, some of James’ comments have made headlines.Despite any drama that it might have caused, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James kept herself away from any mess as she focused on her life and her work.Last year, in May, LeBron James’ wife Savannah James also turned into an entrepreneur as she launched her own brand, Reframe Beauty.Reframe Beauty is a luxury clinical skincare brand and has been pretty successful as Savannah James focuses on new launches and marketing campaigns.For now, the focus remains on the NBA legend LeBron James ahead of his seemingly last season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James’ latest social media message ahead of new NBA season hints hardcore championship chase with Sixers
articles.summary: LeBron James picked an interesting week to remind everyone why the basketball world still watches his every move.
articles.body: LeBron James picked an interesting week to remind everyone why the basketball world still watches his every move. One day before his first training camp as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers, the 41-year-old posted an Instagram message that read like both a thank-you note and a warning shot to the rest of the Eastern Conference.The post came wrapped in gratitude for the people who pushed him through an unusual offseason, one spent adjusting to a new city, a new roster and a fresh set of expectations. It landed the same day as a separate revelation, delivered on a podcast, where James laid out exactly why Philadelphia won him over.LeBron James drops a message on social media ahead of his first season with PhiladelphiaLeBron James, now officially the $8 million forward on Philadelphia's roster, shared his message on Instagram this past Friday, just days before the Sixers open training camp on Tuesday. The post read: "Helluva way to cap off the off season! Appreciate you boys for the vibes every single morning before the sun came up! Year 24 on the way! LET'S GET IT." He also tagged his training crew, crediting @chrisjohnsonhoops, @corysmithhoops and the group at @jus.hoop for getting his body ready for a 24th professional season.Camp opens Tuesday, and the Sixers begin the regular season on Oct. 20 against the defending champion New York Knicks. James joins a lineup built around Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid, plus Jaylen Brown, the two-way wing Philadelphia landed in a trade with Boston this past summer.Why did LeBron James sign with the Philadelphia 76ersJames used a September 25 episode of his "Mind the Game" podcast with Steve Nash to walk through the decision himself. He explained that Maxey, a longtime friend of his sons, was among the first people to call once word got out that he had informed the Lakers he wouldn't return. "I love everything about Tyrese Maxey, man," James said, describing a bond he called rare in sports and in life.The pull toward Philadelphia grew once the Sixers landed Brown in the Boston trade, and it deepened around Embiid. James pointed out that Embiid has accomplished nearly everything the league has to offer except win a title, and said helping him finally get there was part of what drew him east. articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry continue their decade long mission as their foundation Eat, Learn, Play works to help Oakland children
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the NBA icon, and his wife, popular chef and actress, Ayesha Curry, have been active when it comes to looking out for their hometown.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the NBA icon, and his wife, popular chef and actress, Ayesha Curry, have been active when it comes to looking out for their hometown. Both of them have remained committed to it as they have raised millions in the last few years, As Stephen Curry signs an extension worth $116 million with the Golden State Warriors,Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, reflects on the high couple’s efforts to improve things for children across OaklandA few days ago, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, made a heartfelt post about the high profile couple’s efforts for close to a decade.The post read as, “From day one, Stephen and Ayesha committed to personally fund all overhead costs so that 100% of donated and raised funds go directly into our community programs.”The post added, “As an Eat. Learn. Play. partner or donor, every dollar given goes to fund meals, books, tutoring, sports, and schoolyards for Oakland students. As our CEO, Chris Helfrich, says, “change is a team sport.” Seven years in, we’ve got a lot of teammates to thank…”Eat, Learn & Play has worked extensively for the Oakland children ever since it was founded as it looked after the educational and nutritional needs for the ones coming from underprivileged backgrounds.What started as a mission to help children has now expanded into creating more and more opportunities for them.Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry opens up about the lack of opportunities for children in Oakland as they focus on being there for themIn an interview, Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry reflected on their efforts in Oakland as she said, "There is this huge void and they don't have access to the simple things in life, nutritious foods, great education and a safe place to play and so we said we need to change that…”The four time NBA champion added, "I think we are working hard to positively impact as many children as we can, but obviously to do that we need donations because we are a charity," added Curry.Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry continued, "Our goal is to join forces, raise awareness and let people know that there are resources out there and the people just need help and that a little bit goes a really, really long way," she said.With just weeks left for the new season to begin, all eyes are on the Golden State Warriors’ star player Stephen Curry as he recently signed an extension with the team.In the past few months, Stephen Curry has made it clear that he is focused on staying in the Golden State Warriors until he retires and he has no plans of moving to another team.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Así es el negocio de abonados de los clubes de la ACB: de premiar la fidelidad al abono parcial
articles.standfirst: Los equipos preparan reformas o nuevos pabellones, después de que algunos se hayan quedado pequeños ante la creciente masa social de la liga
articles.summary: Los equipos preparan reformas o nuevos pabellones, después de que algunos se hayan quedado pequeños ante la creciente masa social de la liga
articles.body: Las gradas de la Liga Endesa volverán a ser protagonistas en 2026-2027. El número de abonados es uno de los principales termómetros de la demanda por el baloncesto español y, a tenor de los registros agregados, el furor por el deporte de la canasta es cada vez mayor. La masa social de la ACB marcará un nuevo récord esta temporada con 110.717 abonados, un 3% más respecto a la anterior temporada. Los ascensos de Monbus Obradoiro y, especialmente, el de Leyma Coruña han sido claves para impulsar esta cifra, pero también registros históricos en clubes como Valencia Basket, Casademont Zaragoza, Fiatc Girona, Ilerna Lleida o La Laguna Tenerife. De hecho, hasta 13 de los 16 conjuntos que disputaron la pasada edición de la Liga Endesa han mejorado sus registros. La acción sobre el parqué arrancó el pasado fin de semana en una liga que viene de pulverizar su récord de asistencia en 2025-2026, cuando se superaron los 2 millones de espectadores. La ocupación de los pabellones rondó el 75% y la asistencia media fue de 6.807 personas por partido. El listón que deja el curso pasado no parece insalvable, pese a que el descenso de Covirán Granada y Cajasiete Gran Canaria supone la pérdida del décimo y undécimo club con mayor asistencia media y la marcha de pabellones con un aforo de 8.500 y 10.000 personas, respectivamente. Ahora bien, solo con los datos de abonados, Obradoiro y Coruña ya se aproximan a la cifra media de espectadores registrada por los dos descendidos. Además, en cuanto a la media de abonados, esta temporada se ha rebasado por primera vez la barrera de los 6.000 espectadores con un promedio de 6.151 abonados por club La campaña de abonados ha estado marcada por las promociones o descuentos vinculados al uso de los abonos durante la temporada pasada. El objetivo es fomentar la fidelidad, promociones familiares o para grupos, así como modelos alternativos como el acceso parcial y hasta categorías subvencionadas por organismos públicos. La fórmula más extendida consiste en premiar a quien ya estaba dentro. Valencia Basket ha convertido esta política en una de las principales novedades de su campaña, manteniendo las tarifas generales del año pasado pero con una bonificación del 10% para los abonados que cumplían los requisitos de asistencia. El club taronja también tiene en cuenta la cesión del carnet. Unicaja ha seguido una lógica similar. El club costasoleño partía de unos 9.000 abonados la pasada temporada y ha alcanzado una tasa de renovación del 97%, hasta el punto de que no ha necesitado realizar una campaña abierta de captación. Una lista de espera de unas 1.500 personas permitía cubrir las bajas y finalmente ha crecido hasta cerca de 9.300 abonados, manteniendo una parte del aforo disponible para venta de entradas. El presidente del Unicaja de Málaga, Antonio López-Nieto, explica a 2Playbook que “la temporada pasada nos planteamos un grupo de trabajo para incentivar la asistencia per se: si los abonados acuden a los partidos, obtienen un descuento. Había encuentros donde la disponibilidad de entradas era menor y veíamos que muchos abonados no venían, así que hemos buscado fórmulas para fomentar que vengan o cedan su abono, ajustándolo en la oferta de este año”. Uno de los casos más singulares es el de Kids&Us Manresa. El club catalán tiene más del 90% del aforo ya comprometido mediante abonos, que están agotados desde hace varias temporadas. En los últimos años, ha optado por exprimir de otra manera las pocas localidades disponibles. El club divide parte de los asientos restantes en tres bloques de partidos y comercializa abonos parciales. Así, unas 40 localidades pueden generar alrededor de 120 abonados, cada uno con acceso aproximadamente a un tercio de los encuentros. Cada bloque combina partidos de diferente atractivo y se comercializa por un precio equivalente a un tercio del abono convencional. “Es una opción muy competitiva: cuesta una tercera parte del abono normal y da derecho a ver casi un tercio de los partidos de la competición. Está teniendo muy buena acogida y nos permite nuestro gran objetivo, que es sumar a más gente involucrada con el club sin necesidad de ampliar el aforo del pabellón”, señala Carles Sixto, gerente del Kids&Us Manresa. Otra vía de crecimiento pasa por reducir el precio de entrada mediante acuerdos institucionales. Surne Bilbao Basket ha estrenado esta temporada el abono Harmaila Zirkularra, respaldado por la Diputación de Bizkaia con un precio de 145 euros. El producto se concentra en las dos filas superiores del Anillo 4 y está dirigido a aficionados que acrediten un compromiso con la sostenibilidad. Los que adquieran este carnet deberán consumir sólo lo que necesiten, primando el producto sostenible y de kilómetro cero, dar segunda vida a todo lo que se prescinda y depositar sus residuos en contenedores o puntos de recogida de reciclaje. Asisa Joventut, con uno de los pabellones de mayor capacidad en la ACB, también ha puesto el foco en la captación de nuevos aficionados. La entidad ofrece un descuento del 50% en los abonos infantiles cuando se incorpora simultáneamente un adulto y mantiene una promoción para grupos de cuatro personas de entre 17 y 25 años, con un 20% de descuento durante el primer año. Valencia Basket volverá a liderar en abonados en su segunda temporada en el Roig Arena. El vigente campeón de la Liga Endesa cerró la campaña de renovación y nuevas altas con 11.900 abonados, 400 más que hace un año. Precisamente, el club taronja pulverizó en la 2025-2026 los registros de asistencia media con 11.916 espectadores por partido. Tras salvarse sobre la bocina hace pocos meses, Casademont Zaragoza ha establecido un nuevo máximo con 7.175 abonados en una temporada en la que celebra su 25 aniversario. Fiatc Girona también está ante un nuevo mejor registro. La ampliación de Fontajau ha elevado la capacidad hasta superar las 5.600 localidades y le ha permitido superar por primera vez el techo de 4.200 carnés. Las previsiones del club apuntan hacia los 4.500 abonados, récord desde el ascenso a la Liga Endesa. El nuevo diseño del pabellón permite reservar alrededor de un millar de asientos por partido para la venta de entradas. En Lleida, el crecimiento es más limitado en términos absolutos, pero significativo por su tamaño del mercado. El Ilerna Lleida ha elevado el techo de 4.500 a 4.700 abonados. Mientras, el recién ascendido Leyma Coruña ha dado un salto relevante de los 5.825 abonados en Primera FEB a cerca de 7.000 en su vuelta a la élite. La Laguna Tenerife ha superado su propio techo al alcanzar los 4.550 abonados, frente a los 4.511 de la temporada anterior y los 4.203 de hace dos cursos. También con su ascenso, Monbus Obradoiro ha pasado de una base próxima a 4.700 a superar los 5.000. Otros, como Kosner Baskonia, mantienen prácticamente estable su masa social, con unos 8.900 abonados. Recoletas San Pablo Burgos también espera repetir las cifras de hace un año con alrededor de 7.500 abonados, tras contar con más de 6.500 renovaciones en agosto. Muchos clubes ya se están acercando al límite de capacidad de sus pabellones, por lo que la necesidad de nuevas instalaciones empieza a ser una prioridad para poder explotar todo su potencial, tanto en el número de abonados como en la venta de entradas al público general, y la oferta de espacios de hospitality también se está quedando pequeña. La Laguna Tenerife, Kids & Us Manresa y FC Barcelona cuentan con proyectos para la construcción de nuevos pabellones, mientras que Fiatc Girona, Real Madrid y Unicaja de Málaga ya planifican la reforma de sus recintos actuales para ampliar su aforo. “Con la renovación prevista en la instalación para 2027, esperamos superar los 11.200 espectadores en el Martín Carpena. Podremos rascar algo de aforo, pero dentro de unos parámetros realistas: nunca vamos a tener una instalación de 15.000 asientos. Creo que defendemos muy bien el pabellón que tenemos y mantenemos un equilibrio bastante aceptable entre asistencia y facturación”, asegura López-Nieto. El abanico de precios muestra también la diversidad del negocio. MoraBanc Andorra parte del precio estándar más bajo entre los datos disponibles, con 140 euros, mientras que los abonos ordinarios de Valencia Basket pueden alcanzar los 1.300 euros sin tener en cuenta categorías VIP y hospitality. Entre los clubes cuyos precios máximos alcanzan cotas más altas aparecen también Baskonia, Real Madrid y Unicaja con precios alrededor de los 1.000 euros. El FC Barcelona cuenta con la categoría más barata de la competición, valorada en 110 euros por una localidad en la zona 3 superior del Palau Blaugrana, pero el abono de los azulgranas está supeditado al pago previo del carnet de socio de 225 euros. La competición llega a la nueva temporada con una cartera comercial renovada. La principal novedad en este curso es la incorporación de la automovilística china GWM en sustitución de Toyota, con un acuerdo hasta 2029. Otra de las permutas más relevantes es la de Munich por Peak Sports como proveedor de la vestimenta de los colegiados durante las dos próximas campañas y la entrada de Erreà como proveedor técnico oficial y suministrador de la equipación técnica oficial del staff de la ACB mediante una alianza plurianual. La asociación de clubes también ha sumado a su cartera de socios a Intertropic como proveedor oficial de todas sus competiciones a través de las marcas Aguacate y Mango de España con una estrategia dinámica adaptada a la estacionalidad de cada fruta. En el apartado de renovaciones, la ACB ha prolongado la vinculación de Lotus como reloj oficial y a Transaher como proveedor oficial y operador logístico, ambos por otras tres temporadas. El pool de marcas de la competición lo lidera Endesa como patrocinador principal y title sponsor, seguido de GWM, Banco Mediolanum y Pelayo Seguros como patrocinadores oficiales. El otro gran frente de crecimiento es el audiovisual. Al menos en lo que respecta a la visibilidad de la liga. DAZN se mantiene como plataforma principal y ofrecerá la competición íntegra, con un partido en abierto por jornada en su plataforma. Los canales de DAZN se continuarán integrando en Movistar Plus+, Orange TV y Vodafone TV. La gran novedad de esta temporada es el aumento de la presencia en abierto gracias a un mayor despliegue en televisiones autonómicas. A la ventana de TV3 se le suma la TVG gallega, también con un partido a la semana de los clubes de su región, así como Aragón TV y EITB, que ofrecerán diez encuentros por temporada también de clubes de sus respectivas comunidades. El nuevo acuerdo con las televisiones autonómicas de Galicia, Aragón y País Vasco hace referencia a las temporadas 2026-2027 y 2027-2028.

articles.title: El campeón Olympiacos recupera a Bryant Dunston con ¡40 años!
articles.standfirst: El pívot, un ilustre de la Euroliga, y el escolta George Papas firman por los de El Pireo hasta final de temporada
articles.summary: El pívot, un ilustre de la Euroliga, y el escolta George Papas firman por los de El Pireo hasta final de temporada
articles.body: Hace tiempo, seguir jugando al baloncesto con 35 años era una proeza. Ahora es de lo más normal. Los cuidados físicos que tienen los jugadores, con cuerpos médicos y tratamientos a su disposición; la alimentación, un aspecto que cada vez se cuida más; hasta la evolución de las zapatillas... Muchos son los detalles para que se alarguen las carreras y jugadores veteranos sigan en pista con un rol importante e incluso sean protagonistas de operaciones en el mercado. En el loco verano que se ha vivido en la Euroliga, han sido traspasados Patty Mills (al ASVEL con 38), Kenneth Faried (al Baskonia con 36 años), Will Clyburn (al Fenerbahce con 36), Mike James (al Anadolu Efes con 36), Nikola Mirotic (al Valencia Basket con 35)... Con 34 años o cerca de cumplirlos, Toko Shengelia, Thomas Walkup, Shane Larkin, Tomas Satoransky, Daniel Theis, Moustapha Fall, Jonas Valanciunas... Pero el Olympiacos, campeón de la Euroliga, ha superado todas esas marcas con el regreso de viejo conocidos del club. El pívot Bryant Dunston, a sus 40 años, regresa a El Pireo con un contrato hasta el final de la campaña después de haber hecho la pretemporada con el equipo de un Giorgios Bartzokas al que ha terminado por convencer. El veteranísimo jugador se suma a un juego interior que ya dispone de Nikola Milutinov, Donta Hall y Tyrique Jones. Habrá que ver el rendimiento que puede dar en una competición cada año más exigente en lo físico. La temporada pasada, jugando en Milán, tuvo medias de 2,9 puntos y 2,1 rebotes en casi 11 minutos en los 17 encuentros que disputó. Dunston es un ilustre de la Euroliga con pasado en el club heleno (2013-15), el Anadolu Efes, con el que fue dos veces campeón continental, la Virtus, el Zalgiris y el Armani Milán. El pívot de 2,03 metros, una roca en sus mejores tiempos, lideró la competición en tapones y fue nombrado mejor defensor en 2014 y 2015. El Olympiacos también ha anunciado la contratación de George Papas, exterior greco-estadounidense que igualmente tuvo una etapa anterior en el equipo entre 2022 y 2024.

articles.title: LeBron James desvela por culpa de qué jugador decidió fichar por los Sixers
articles.standfirst: LeBron James le cuenta a Steve Nash que no quiso hablar con otros jugadores durante su proceso tras dejar los Lakers para finalmente elegir a los Sixers
articles.summary: LeBron James le cuenta a Steve Nash que no quiso hablar con otros jugadores durante su proceso tras dejar los Lakers para finalmente elegir a los Sixers
articles.body: LeBron James le confesó a Steve Nash su proceso para elegir los Philadelphia 76ers tras dejar Los Angeles Lakers para convertirse en agente libre. La nueva estrella de los Sixers desveló en el podcast 'Mind the Game' que mientras se decidía evitó hablar con otros jugadores: "Ni siquiera quiero que me influyan en una dirección u otra". 'King James' reconoce que cuando vio en su teléfono el nombre de Tyrese Maxey (25 años), su nuevo compañero en Philadelphia, no pudo evitar contestar. "Cuando me convertí en agente libre y decidimos comunicarles a los Lakers que no iba a regresar, Maxey fue una de las primeras personas en llamarme: 'Oye, ¿qué vamos a hacer? ¿Qué tal, veterano? Vente para aquí, hombre; ¡nos vendrías muy bien aquí!'... Es una persona tan estupenda que no puedo dejar de hablar con él", explicó. LeBron James compartió que "mi relación con Tyrese Maxey va más allá de la pista. Simplemente me encanta todo de Tyrese Maxey. Cada día te encuentras con la misma persona. Y eso es algo muy poco común en el deporte y extremadamente raro en la vida. Siempre he hablado de la gran persona que es. Y, por supuesto, sabemos lo que aporta a la cancha de baloncesto". "Ha sido la misma persona desde el momento en que lo conocí, antes de que fuera seleccionado en el Draft de la NBA. Vino a mi casa; en aquel entonces tenía 19 años, así que pasaba el rato con mis hijos Bronny y Bryce. Jugaban a videojuegos. Llegó mostrándose muy respetuoso conmigo, con mi esposa y con todos los que estaban en la casa. Siempre con una sonrisa radiante y una actitud muy sencilla y cercana. Desde el momento en que fue seleccionado hasta convertirse en la superestrella constante que es hoy, nada ha cambiado. Su actitud sigue intacta. Todos sabemos cómo ocurre a veces: llega un chico humilde, alcanza cierto éxito y cambia por completo. Pero él ha seguido siendo la misma persona. Sin duda, este joven demuestra una madurez impropia de su edad. Es fácil querer apoyarlo", apuntó. LeBron James también destacó la presencia de un MVP como Joel Embiid en los Sixers: "Lo ha logrado todo en nuestra liga. Lo único que le falta es ganar un campeonato. Quiero intentar ayudarle a conseguir ese primer título. Ha sido MVP de la liga, tiene una medalla de oro, ha sido All-Star, tiene sus propias zapatillas, muchísimo dinero... lo tiene todo". articles.summary: El base del Kids&Us Manresa recibió un fuerte golpe en el pecho durante el partido de este sábado ante el Surne Bilbao
articles.body: El Kids&Us Manresa ha informado este lunes de la hospitalización de Hugo Benítez. Este sábado, el base francés sufrió un neumotórax provocado por un fuerte golpe en el pecho durante el partido que su equipo disputó en Miribilla ante el Surne Bilbao Basket. El club no ha especificado un posible tiempo de baja. El conjunto manresano ha añadido que Benítez se encuentra hospitalizado y se está recuperándose de una pequeña intervención quirúrgica. El neumotórax es una acumulación anormal de aire en el espacio pleural, entre el pulmón y la pared torácica, que ejerce presión sobre el pulmón y provoca su colapso parcial o total. La dolencia de Benítez añade un nuevo problema al conjunto manresano, que en el debut ante el Bilbao no pudo contar con Timmy Allen y Pierre Oriola. articles.title: NBA veteran Lamar Odom takes dig at ESPN NBA rankings, reveals why Jalen Brunson should be No 1 or 2 over Nikola Jokic
articles.summary: Lamar Odom has questioned ESPN’s Top 100 NBA Players list for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body: Lamar Odom has questioned ESPN’s Top 100 NBA Players list for the 2026-27 season. The former Los Angeles Lakers star believes Jalen Brunson deserves to be much higher after helping the New York Knicks win the NBA championship. Brunson was ranked No. 6 on ESPN’s top 10, while Nikola Jokić took the No. 1 spot.Odom made his feelings clear when TMZ Sports caught up with him at LAX. He particularly disagreed with Brunson’s position on the list. Odom argued that a player who has won a championship should not be ranked so low. He also revealed his own top five, placing Brunson at No. 1.Lamar Odom puts Jalen Brunson ahead of Nikola JokicLamar Odom did not hold back when asked about ESPN’s rankings. He questioned how Brunson could be ranked outside the top five after winning a championship with the Knicks.“How you gon’ be six if you won a championship?” Odom questioned. Gotta be one or two,” the ex- LA Laker icon said.Brunson was listed at No. 6 in ESPN’s top 10 players for the 2026-27 season. That ranking puts him behind several established stars and some of the league’s biggest young talents.Odom’s personal list looked very different. He put Brunson at No. 1, followed by Victor Wembanyama, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić and Giannis Antetokounmpo.ESPN’s list has Jokić at No. 1. The Denver Nuggets star is followed by Victor Wembanyama at No. 2 and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at No. 3. Luka Dončić is fourth, while Giannis Antetokounmpo completes the top five.Jalen Brunson is sixth, followed by Anthony Edwards at No. 7. Cade Cunningham is eighth, Jayson Tatum is ninth and Donovan Mitchell rounds out the top 10.The rankings also marked a notable change for James. The former Los Angeles Lakers star fell outside the top five and was ranked 18th. It is the first time he has been outside ESPN’s top 10 in the history of the list.ESPN also changed the way its rankings were decided this year. Seven ESPN experts voted on the 2026-27 rankings instead of using the larger panel seen in previous editions.The rankings are based on predicted individual performance and contributions during the regular season. They are not simply a ranking of a player’s entire career or past achievements.That distinction could explain some of the differences between Odom’s view and ESPN’s list. Odom placed strong importance on Brunson’s championship success, while ESPN’s criteria focus on expected regular-season impact for the upcoming campaign.Odom also acknowledged how difficult it is to rank the league’s best players, “It’s hard. They’re all great.”The debate is likely to continue once the new NBA season begins. articles.title: De Larrea ya tiene padrino en Dallas: "Vamos con él, queremos que triunfe"
articles.standfirst: Kyrie Irving, líder del vestuario de los Mavericks, alaba la actitud del novato español
articles.summary: Kyrie Irving, líder del vestuario de los Mavericks, alaba la actitud del novato español
articles.body: Sergio De Larrea está a las puertas de su estreno en la NBA. El base español, elegido por los Mavericks en el puesto 25 del último draft, ya está metido en la dinámica de la franquicia. Se le ha visto jugando al golf con el resto de sus compañeros, entrenando con ellos en la playa y también en la pista. Sobre todo ahí, está muy pendiente de Kyrie Irving, al que tiene como uno de sus referentes en el equipo. 'Larry', como ya le conocen en Dallas, considera a Irving "un líder no sólo como jugador, sino como persona. Está intentando enseñar lo que ha hecho hasta ahora en las 15 temporadas que ha estado en la NBA, intenta enseñar esto a los nuevos, a todos los que estamos aquí. Quiero aprender cómo hace las cosas en un entorno tan complicado y competitivo. Es perfecto tenerle, aprender de él e intentar desarrollar mi juego de esa manera". Tras los elogios del español, la réplica del estadounidense nacido en Melbourne. "Le di mil dólares para que lo dijera", bromeó Irving antes de decir que "De Larrea es un chico que ya tiene un gran conocimiento del juego. Es un ganador que viene de un equipo con mentalidad ganadora en Europa y se nota que tiene hambre por aprender. Quiere empaparse de todo y progresar rápido. Podrá apoyarse en mí siempre que quiera. Vamos con él, queremos que triunfe, y él se está vaciando para conseguirlo". Irving volverá a jugar después de haberse perdido más de una temporada. Su último encuentro fue el 3 de marzo de 2025. El base se rompió el ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla izquierda, pero ya está recuperado y no tiene restricciones de entrenamiento ni minutos. El 21 de octubre debería estar listo para el estreno cuando los Mavericks visiten a los Rockets. "Estoy listo para salir y patear unos cuantos culos", sentencia. Por sus palabras, el base parece en plenitud tanto física como mentalmente. "Sé que los rumores acerca de cómo voy a rendir son inevitables, pero ahora mismo tengo la confianza de un campeón. Esta es una Liga en la que sólo cuenta lo que has hecho recientemente, así que tengo muchas ganas de atarme las zapatillas y estar en la pista con mis compañeros para recordarle a todo el mundo lo que puedo hacer. Será como montar en bicicleta", asegura. Al contrario que otros jugadores a los que una lesión de larga duración hunde en un oscuro agujero, Irving afirma que "la lesión es probablemente lo mejor que me ha pasado". El base vuelve a demostrar que tiene un carácter y una personalidad especial. "Estaba obsesionándome con el baloncesto y con jugar la mayoría de minutos. Si en aquel momento me hubieseis preguntado cómo me sentía a nivel físico y cómo estaba gestionando tanta carga, mi respuesta no habría sido sincera", dice. En el tiempo de baja que ha tenido, Irving cuenta que ha reflexionado sobre "cómo quiero ser como jugador y como persona. Cómo puedo hacer que me vean como un mejor líder y un mejor comunicador, mostrarme más emocional y vulnerable. Y también cómo empezar a actuar acorde a mi edad. A mis 34 años, a punto de empezar mi decimosexta temporada, he pasado por muchas cosas, por muchos altos y bajos. Pero como competidor nadie tiene que tener dudas de que voy a hacer lo que corresponda". Es el liderazgo que admira De Larrea.

The Golden State Valkyries beat the Dallas Wings , 104-80, in the first game of the team's first round WNBA playoff series on Sunday. Gabby Williams scored 20 points to go along with four assists, three rebounds and a steal in a team-high, low stress 27 minutes.

That's like my favorite rapper when I was a kid. So my whole family group chat was going crazy that I did that. So that made me happy."

Williams and the Valkyries will now have two days off to travel to Dallas for Game 2 where they can end the series. If the Wings win, they'll be back in the Bay on Friday for Game 3.

articles.title: Lynx's Olivia Miles Wins 2026 WNBA ROY Award After Historic Season, Full Voting Results
articles.summary: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles was the unanimous pick for Rookie of the Year following a record-setting season.
articles.body:
Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles was the unanimous pick for Rookie of the Year following a record-setting season.

Miles averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 1.3 steals while shooting 49.2 percent overall and 38.8 percent from beyond the arc. Her 790 total points were the most ever for a WNBA rookie.

Miles was considered by some to be the best player in the 2026 WNBA draft class, though she went second overall behind UConn sharpshooter Azzi Fudd. Passing on the former Notre Dame and TCU star is looking like a major whiff by the Dallas Wings.

With five collegiate seasons under her belt, the 5'10" playmaker arrived in the WNBA as a polished prospect. Nobody envisioned her making the kind of impact she did straight out of the gate, though.

Many assumed the Lynx would tread water a bit with star Napheesa Collier recovering from offseason ankle surgery. She didn't make her season debut until July 22.

Thanks to Miles' efforts, Minnesota compiled a 22-6 record by the time Collier was back on the court. The rookie more than rose to the occasion and occupied a leadership role on the floor in Collier's absence.

Miles effectively had Rookie of the Year wrapped up within the first few months. Fudd's season-ending knee surgery cleared the runway even more.

The timing of Monday's announcement is a little unfortunate as it comes a day after Minnesota dropped Game 1 of its first-round playoff series against the New York Liberty. For once, Miles showed her inexperience as she shot 3-of-12 from the field and had four turnovers to one assist.

Even if the Lynx fall short of reaching the WNBA Finals for the second time in three years, the 2026 campaign should be considered a success because they discovered a new franchise cornerstone.

articles.title: Lynx's Cheryl Reeve Wins 2026 WNBA Coach of the Year Award, Full Voting Results
articles.summary: Cheryl Reeve is the WNBA Coach of the Year for the fifth time, extending her league record.
articles.body:
Cheryl Reeve is the WNBA Coach of the Year for the fifth time, extending her league record.

The Minnesota Lynx coach received 40 of the 74 first-place votes. The Golden State Valkyries' Natalie Nakase was runner-up with 20 votes, and Washington Mystics coach Sydney Johnson was third on the ballot.

Caitlin Gives Fever Performance 'an F' 😬

The Lynx finished with the WNBA's best record, going 33-11. As consistent as the franchise has been through the years, Minnesota was far from a favorite to claim the No. 1 seed.

In Bleacher Report's power rankings ahead of opening night, Hunter Cruse had the Lynx down in fourth.

Two key players in the frontcourt, co-Defensive Player of the Year Alanna Smith and Jessica Shepard, signed with the Dallas Wings. Natisha Hiedeman, the runner-up for Sixth Player of the Year, also bolted for the Seattle Storm.

Compounding matters, Napheesa Collier had offseason ankle surgery that kept her off the court until late July.

Despite everything working against the Lynx, they set the bar for the rest of the league.

Olivia Miles flourished in her rookie season. The 5'10" playmaker possesses plenty of talent, but part of her success is undoubtedly owed to Reeve's coaching.

The same goes for Natasha Howard making her first All-Star team since 2022. She shot a career-best 59.8 percent from the field and helped fill the void left by Smith and Shepard.

Nakase has worked wonders with the Valkyries. They've made the playoffs in each of their first two years in the WNBA, and their record in 2026 improved by nine wins.

Johnson took the youngest roster in the league and guided the Mystics to 28 wins, their most in a single season.

Either would've been a worthy candidate for Coach of the Year, but nobody will argue with Reeve's victory.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Won't Take Questions on NBA Investigation at Raptors Media Day After Clippers Trade
articles.summary: Toronto Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard opened his media day appearance on Monday by declaring that he won't take questions regarding the NBA's investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers' alleged salary cap circumvention.
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors star forward Kawhi Leonard opened his media day appearance on Monday by declaring that he won't take questions regarding the NBA's investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers' alleged salary cap circumvention.

"I'm excited to be here. I know why some of you guys came, you want to hear about the investigation," Leonard told reporters. "But talking with the NBA and the PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor. I already was a distraction for the past 70 days. ... Moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors today."

Leonard referred to his previous statement on the NBA's investigation in which he said through his agent that he accepted "full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family."

"I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone's part to circumvent the salary cap," he added.

The Clippers incurred severe punishments that included the loss of five future first-round draft picks, a fine of $30 million and a year-long suspension of team owner Steve Ballmer. After initially disputing the penalties, Ballmer announced that he would accept the one-year ban.

After a delay due to the investigation, the Raptors sent forward Brandon Ingram, guard Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap and two second-rounders to the Clippers to acquire Leonard, who later agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with Toronto plus a player option for the 2028-29 season.

Leonard has been known to be a man of few words, so it's not a surprise that he's not interested in discussing the offseason controversy as he tries to move forward with the Raptors.

articles.title: La Euroliga se ayudará de Inteligencia Artificial en la designación de los árbitros
articles.standfirst: La IA decidirá los colegiados más adecuados en base a una serie de parámetros como la jerarquía arbitral, el calendario, la nacionalidad de equipos y el contexto del partido
articles.summary: La IA decidirá los colegiados más adecuados en base a una serie de parámetros como la jerarquía arbitral, el calendario, la nacionalidad de equipos y el contexto del partido
articles.body: Los árbitros de los partidos de Euroliga y Eurocup serán designados desde esta temporada con la ayuda de la Inteligencia Artificial. Las dos competiciones más importantes del baloncesto europeo utilizarán un sistema automatizado y que cuenta con la última tecnología para decidir qué tres árbitros pitarán cada encuentro. No será la IA a su libre albedrío quien decida las designaciones sino que decidirá en base a una amplia gama de criterios establecidos por el Departamento de Arbitraje de Baloncesto de la Euroliga, dirigido por el excolegiado español Daniel Hierrezuelo. Entre ellos está la jerarquía arbitral, el calendario de la competición, las asignaciones previas, la nacionalidad de equipos y colegiados, la carga de trabajo y el contexto del partido. Mediante el análisis de toda la información disponible, el sistema aplica 14 reglas diferentes agrupadas en tres áreas clave: criterios deportivos, gestión del calendario y la carga de trabajo, e integridad. Esto permite al sistema determinar las asignaciones arbitrales más adecuadas para cada partido en cada jornada de competición. "La tecnología nos brinda la oportunidad de llevar el proceso de asignación de árbitros a otro nivel, permitiéndonos analizar una gran cantidad de información y aplicar un conjunto coherente de criterios a cada partido", declaró Daniel Hierrezuelo, director de arbitraje de la Euroliga. "Nuestro objetivo es utilizar la innovación para apoyar el trabajo de nuestros árbitros, optimizar la distribución de las asignaciones y la carga de trabajo a lo largo de la temporada y garantizar que se tenga en cuenta cada factor relevante al conformar cada equipo arbitral", explica el excolegiado. Desde la Euroliga se considera que la introducción del nuevo sistema representa un paso más en el compromiso constante con la innovación y la mejora continua de sus procesos de competición. Además, se asegura que el modelo de designación está diseñado para garantizar una distribución equilibrada de las asignaciones arbitrales, manteniendo al mismo tiempo los más altos estándares de coherencia, transparencia e imparcialidad. Este nuevo sistema de designación de árbitros se implementó con éxito por primera vez en el estreno de la Euroliga la semana pasada y se introducirá en la EuroCup a partir de la jornada inaugural de la próxima semana.

articles.title: Everything Jalen Brunson Said About Knicks' NBA Title, SNL, Mitchell Robinson Exit, More
articles.summary: Winning a championship isn't without some drawbacks.
articles.body:
Winning a championship isn't without some drawbacks.

During the New York Knicks' media day Monday, star guard Jalen Brunson reflected on how he had the "longest, shortest summer ever." The team's NBA Finals triumph brought added obligations and appearances, eating into some of Brunson's offseason.

One such example was the three-time All-Star's recent hosting gig on Saturday Night Live . He said it's too soon for him to fully reflect on his performance:

Brunson is familiar with turning around and trying to defend a title. He was a two-time national champion at Villanova. He stressed the need to remain focused and not coast on what happened last year, and he believes his teammates will understand that objective:

The Knicks are mostly running it back. Mitchell Robinson was their only notable exit, with Andre Drummond taking his place in the frontcourt. While he was disappointed to see Robinson go, Brunson is confident in Drummond's ability to provide depth at center:

It will be fascinating to see which version of the Knicks shows up in 2026-27: the one that won 53 games and finished third in the Eastern Conference, or the one that turned into an unstoppable machine in the playoffs.

Prior to the title triumph, a lot of people questioned New York's title credentials.

The Athletic's Sam Amick reported in April that speculation over the future of head coach Mike Brown "won't die down unless they reach the NBA Finals, and even that might not be good enough for the first-year New York coach to be safe."

Now, nobody is questioning whether Brown is the right man for the job or if the Knicks have a championship-caliber roster.

A lot has to go right for a team to win a title, and the challenge becomes even more difficult once you've pulled it off. Brunson is well aware of that, and it's a message he'll continue to convey to the locker room.

articles.title: Draymond Green Reveals LeBron James Recruiting Pitch, Says Warriors Would've Been 'Right Decision'
articles.summary: Draymond Green did his best to persuade LeBron James to the Golden State Warriors in free agency, but in the end, his efforts weren't enough as James joined the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Draymond Green did his best to persuade LeBron James to the Golden State Warriors in free agency, but in the end, his efforts weren't enough as James joined the Philadelphia 76ers.

Green recently explained his recruiting pitch on Open Season on Draymond Green (h/t Andscape's Marc J. Spears ):

"I told him all the great things. How cool would it be for him to join Steph, who's pretty much carried the NBA for the better of the last 15 years, 'Bron a little longer, but they are 'the guys.' And how cool would it be to [challenge] these young guys who are kind of taking over? Their time is up now to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and all these [young] guys. How cool would it be for the two guys who's battled on the biggest stage for so many years in the NBA who now see these younger guys taking over, just for one time to say, 'Hey, fellas, we can still do this. Yeah, move over'? How dope would that be?

"Everybody speaks about the basketball side. Most people don't understand how important it is to have teammates that you rock with at this age. Teammates that are like-minded. Teammates that have similar lives. Teammates that when you go to dinner, you want to go to dinner and sit with. As you get older in this league, that becomes a weird thing. We'll have that. This will be the greatest show on Earth, by the way. Stephen and LeBron together?

"How much has [James] gotten into golf? There's no better place to be for golf than San Francisco. I also thought from a business standpoint, there's a whole business side of business that he hasn't tapped into [in Silicon Valley]. From a business standpoint, what can that mean? I know for sure this would be the best organization you've ever played in. I know that for certain."

Green noted, though, that James' history against the Warriors may have stopped him from coming to the Bay Area, even if Green thought it'd be the "right decision":

"He just couldn't get over the past, which is, 'I battled these guys over and over again. What is that now going to look like for me if I come there? What type of beating am I going to take if I come there?' And ultimately that's why it didn't happen. … I also think that's why it took so long to make the decision, because I know this [Golden State] was the right decision. He just couldn't land on it."

James, of course, played in four straight NBA Finals against the Warriors during the 2010s while he was a member of the Cleveland Cavaliers. Golden State won three of those matchups, though James and Cleveland pulled off a historic 3-1 comeback in 2016 to upset the 73-win Warriors.

With that type of history, it's possible James may have felt joining Curry and Green may not have been the best decision.

Instead, James will team up with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe in Philadelphia after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers. With a star-studded roster, James will now attempt to win a championship with a fourth team.

articles.title: Everything Karl-Anthony Towns Said About Weight Loss, Knicks Contract Talks, More
articles.summary: If the camera adds 10 pounds, perhaps the Larry O'Brien Trophy subtracts it and more.
articles.body:
If the camera adds 10 pounds, perhaps the Larry O'Brien Trophy subtracts it and more.

After all, New York Knicks big man Karl-Anthony Towns looked slim during Monday's media day ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season. He told reporters "my wife thought I looked good" and that the weight loss "keeps him young."

It was a big offseason for Towns, as he married Jordyn Woods in Malibu at a ceremony that included teammates Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart as guests.

"I couldn't have a wedding without Larry," he said Monday while revealing he brought the championship trophy on dates with him as well.

The Knicks earned that trophy by defeating the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals in five thrilling games. They overcame double-digit deficits, won Game 4 with a thrilling OG Anunoby tip at the buzzer and ended a championship drought for the franchise that dated back to 1973.

Towns' defense on Victor Wembanyama and double-double average of 13.0 points and 10.6 rebounds a night in the series played a major role in the championship and made him a Knicks legend forever.

But he is not signed forever, as this is the final season of his contract before a 2027-28 player option.

He told reporters Monday "there's no comfortability to be had," when discussing whether he was comfortable with contract talks going into the regular season.

Towns' contract status figures to be a major storyline as the Knicks look to defend their title during a new campaign that starts Oct. 20 against the Philadelphia 76ers.

Still, it would be anything but surprising if he and the team eventually come to terms on a deal, as he is a primary reason the Knicks are atop the NBA mountaintop.

Philadelphia 76ers star forward LeBron James sported his new No. 23 jersey at Monday's media day before speaking glowingly about star center Joel Embiid.

"Jo is one of the most talented guys we have in the world," James told reporters . "… For him, it's all about health. … I see he's put in a lot of work on his body, put in a lot of work on his game, put in a lot of work on his mentals this offseason."

When asked about his expected role in his first year in Philadelphia, James responded , "Whatever they need me to do. The luxury of my game is I can do everything. … Literally, I can do everything."

James is joining a Sixers team that is expected to be one of the top contenders for the NBA championship thanks to fellow stars Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, the latter of whom was acquired from the Boston Celtics this offseason. Philadelphia also has rising star guard VJ Edgecombe, who is coming off an All-Rookie first team selection.

James previously said during an episode of his Mind the Game podcast that helping Embiid achieve postseason success was one of the driving forces behind his decision to sign with the Sixers. Despite the big man being one of the most dominant forces in the game, he hasn't been able to lead Philadelphia past the second round of the playoffs throughout his injury-riddled career.

"He's done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said of Embiid. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into The Process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

On Monday, James made it clear that he was motivated to bring an NBA championship to the City of Brotherly Love.

"I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round, I know that," he told reporters .

The 41-year-old also confirmed that he chose the Sixers over four other teams he considered in free agency this summer:

Despite the high expectations he's facing in his first year in Philadelphia, James told reporters that he knows it will be a process for him and his new teammates to get used to one another.

"It's going to take time," he said. "… Everyone wants instant oatmeal. … If you want something special, it takes time and every single day, doing something that you may not want to do."

articles.title: NBA Pressure Rankings: Who faces the most heat this season?
articles.summary: With NBA training camps opening, here are 10 people around the league who have a lot on the line in 2026-27.
articles.body:
Training camp is the time of year when everybody in the NBA gets to believe things will be different. But some people need more than a good media day. They need a season that changes the conversation about their careers, validates their decisions, or convinces their bosses to keep paying them. Another disappointing year could mean losing a championship opportunity, control of a franchise, or a job.

Welcome to the NBA Pressure Rankings. We're choosing from players, coaches and front office executives to figure out the 10 people feeling the most heat entering this season.

Durant will be 38 when the season begins. He has two rings, two Finals MVPs and a résumé that puts him among the greatest players ever. Things could be worse. But falling short in Oklahoma City , Brooklyn and Phoenix has only emboldened the critics who say he rode Golden State 's coattails to championships he couldn't win anywhere else. Winning in Houston would change that conversation. But how many more chances will he get?

Houston won 52 games despite missing Fred VanVleet all season and losing Steven Adams midway through it. Durant helped carry the Rockets through 78 games before knee and ankle injuries limited him to one appearance in their first-round loss to the Lakers . Better health offers reason for optimism. But Houston's reluctance to make a competitive offer for Giannis Antetokounmpo suggests preserving its young core remains the priority.

If this season turns sour, the veterans could be the ones on the block. That includes KD. After last season's unconfirmed allegations that he disparaged teammates through a burner account, another ugly ending would put his leadership under even more scrutiny. Durant could be starting over again with another failed stop on his record and even less time left to win.

After blowing a 3-1 lead in the first round, the Magic fired Jahmal Mosley and hired Sean Sweeney as head coach. But the roster was kept largely the same with only Nikola Vučević replacing Moe Wagner . That's it, seriously! Orlando is betting that a new coach can produce substantially different results with essentially the same players.

Better health would help. Franz Wagner missed the final three games against Detroit . Maybe Mosley would even still be the coach if Wagner stayed on the floor. But let's assume Sweeney changes the system and the core stays healthy. What happens if the end result is still the same: mid-40s wins, inconsistent play from Wagner and Paolo Banchero , and another early playoff exit?

Well, the scrutiny could shift from the coach's choices to the executive who put the team together. Weltman already spent four firsts and a swap to acquire Desmond Bane to fix Orlando's woeful 3-point shooting. It helped, but not enough. So if a major trade and a coaching change aren't enough, what's next?

Weltman's recent contract extension suggests that ownership trusts him to find the answer. But job security won't make decisions any easier. Would a minor move be enough? Or would Banchero and Wagner have to get split up? Odds are something's gonna have to change. Let's see what Weltman has up his sleeve.

Zion played 62 games last season. The Pelicans won 26. Better availability was a nice thing to see from a notoriously injured star. Are we sure Zion can be the best player on a playoff team?

Williamson is a bowling ball at the rim, whether he's creating off the dribble or finishing a cut or roll. But he remains reluctant to shoot.

"It's not that I don't want to shoot them, I just hate when I miss," Williamson told reporters in February. Nice of Zion to admit how he really feels, but he said the same exact thing to me in an interview in 2022. Four years ago! You gotta get over it at some point.

As a 70% guy from the line with soft touch in the paint, he has the potential to become a competent perimeter shooter. So Zion might hate missing shots, but it might be necessary for the Pelicans to start winning.

When I visited Denver after its 2023 championship, then-Nuggets general manager Calvin Booth was talking about building a dynasty. The Nuggets haven't been out of the second round since. Booth was fired at the end of the 2024-25 NBA season on the same day as longtime head coach Michael Malone.

Team president Josh Kroenke deserves scrutiny for what happens to the roster around Nikola Jokić . But if Denver falls short once again, it won't be the son of the owner on the hot seat. It'll be Ben Tenzer, Denver's executive vice president of basketball operations.

With an injury-prone starting group and a shallow bench, the Nuggets are looking less and less like a potential dynasty as the rest of the West ascends. Kroenke should feel pressure to raise more banners as long as Jokić is in Denver. But it's Tenzer who has to worry about what happens if they don't.

Duren followed an All-NBA season with a disastrous postseason. His scoring plummeted from 19.5 points per game to 10.2, and his field-goal percentage dropped from 65 to 51.4. By Game 5 against the Cavaliers, Paul Reed was playing the entire fourth quarter and overtime while Duren watched from the bench.

Pistons media day is today, and Duren remains unsigned after a long summer of contract negotiations. Earlier this month, The Athletic's Sam Amick reported that Detroit offered five years and $190 million, but Duren wants at least $200 million. And if he doesn't get it, he's considering taking the $9.6 million qualifying offer to become an unrestricted free agent next summer. That's quite a gamble!

The Pistons are building around Cade Cunningham , but the team will experience another crash landing in the playoffs unless Duren proves last year's breakout was sustainable and carries it into the playoffs — no matter what contract he signs. If not, the Pistons will be on the lookout for a different kind of center to pair with Cunningham.

"If you know Steve and know Steve's integrity, you know there's nothing to it," Frank said in April about the investigation into the Clippers. Months later, investigators used Frank's own detailed notes to document Steve Ballmer's involvement in helping Kawhi Leonard obtain outside income.

Frank has long been rumored to be the Indiana student manager who secretly recorded Bob Knight's infamous 1991 locker room rant. When Frank was an assistant coach for the Nets in 2013, head coach Jason Kidd removed him from the bench because of rumors that Frank was undermining Kidd. Frank has vehemently denied any involvement in the Knight controversy , and the Kidd drama has never been confirmed. But Frank's role in documenting Ballmer's private conversations is right there in the investigative report, and investigators credited Frank for cooperating, giving consistent answers, and accepting responsibility.

Investigators also identified Frank as one of the three people most responsible for the Clippers breaking NBA rules, and as a result Ballmer was suspended for one year and fined $30 million, the Clippers lost five first-round picks, and Frank received a six-month suspension. Frank deserves credit for helping investigators establish what happened, but how might Ballmer perceive Frank's actions?

Once Frank returns, he'll need to show that he has a credible plan for the Clippers after Kawhi with fewer draft assets available to improve the roster. Ballmer already knows he can't trust Frank as far as he can throw him. So if Ballmer returns and decides the franchise needs a fresh start, Frank will have to convince him that he's the right guy for the job.

Not long ago, Morant looked like a future face of the NBA. This summer, Memphis traded him to Portland for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray . That return tells you how much his value has fallen.

But now Ja has two years left on his contract and a fresh start. He needs to stay available, regain his rhythm, and give the Blazers a reason to keep him around for the long haul. Another shaky season would make his next contract a much different discussion.

I've always been a James Harden admirer. But even Harden's stans have to admit his disappearing acts have cannibalized the conversation about his greatest qualities. Harden is one of the most innovative point guards in league history and he's authored plenty of incredible playoff moments. But what's his reputation? "Choker."

The Cavaliers took 14 games to get through the inexperienced Raptors and the flawed Pistons. Then the Knicks swept them, erased a 22-point fourth-quarter deficit in the opener, and won the finale by 37. In the two Game 7s that Cleveland won, Harden combined for 27 points on 5-for-19 shooting. Then in the East finals, Harden averaged 16 points, shot 17.9% from 3, and had 17 turnovers to only 12 assists. The way Harden performed, and the way Cleveland lost, made it hard to feel any good about how the year went.

Winning a championship in Cleveland wouldn't change the past, but it certainly would change the way people talk about Harden's legacy. The East is open enough for the Cavaliers to have a real shot. But at age 37, time is ticking away.

Jeanie Buss has been Pelinka's most important ally. She hired him to run the Lakers, and their relationship gave him protection through all the ups and downs. But with a second ownership transition underway, Jeanie's power has dwindled.

Pelinka's authority was already facing scrutiny under Mark Walter, who brought in Dodgers executives Andrew Friedman and Farhan Zaidi as advisers. Now that Walter has sold the team, new owners Josh Kushner and Bob Iger could want their own people running basketball operations.

Pelinka remains in charge for now though, and he replaced LeBron James with a roster that, on paper, makes sense around Luka Dončić .

This summer, the Lakers traded two firsts and two swaps for center Walker Kessler , plus added Cameron Carr, Quentin Grimes , Collin Sexton , and Sandro Mamukelashvili . Luka has a center to throw lobs to, shooters to find when help comes, and other guards who can create a shot without him. Austin Reaves is also back on a four-year, $185 million deal. The Lakers outscored opponents by 9.9 points per 100 possessions with him and Luka together last season, per DataBallr.

Who protects the rim if Kessler gets hurt? The Lakers have little reliable depth behind him, and too few wings who can contribute at both ends. Offense won't be a problem in Los Angeles , but defense certainly could be the cause of death come playoff time. Another early exit wouldn't necessarily mean Pelinka deserves to lose his job. But the new owners might decide they trust someone else to build around Luka.

Orbital fractures. Concussions. Knee tendinitis. A torn meniscus. A torn thumb ligament. Bell's palsy. Appendicitis. We're past "Embiid is injury prone." We're in "Embiid is cursed" territory when you factor in the Sixers traded up to take Markelle Fultz , traded away future champion Mikal Bridges on draft night for Zhaire Smith , whose career was derailed by a peanut allergy, and then there was the Ben Simmons era. There was the four-bouncer on the rim with Kawhi Leonard's Game 7 shot in 2019. Hell, the Sixers even lost a GM to his wife's burner accounts!

LeBron chose Philly, Maxey keeps getting better, and Edgecombe could be ready for a bigger role. Nick Nurse should have enough scoring and depth to give Embiid more nights off and ask less of him when he plays. Maybe the Sixers can finally get him through a season without needing him to carry them.

But if Embiid gets hurt anyway? Bob Myers and Mike Gansey will have to decide how many more seasons they're willing to stake on his health. They're new here. For fans who lived through the Process and everything that followed, moving on from Embiid would be much harder. But maybe for the front office, a trade gets the Sixers closer to a championship. I'd still hate to see Embiid spend all those years trying to win in Philly only to watch them finally do it without him.

articles.title: Wemby Says It's Been 'Hard to Fall Asleep' After NBA FInals Loss to Knicks, Talks Motivation
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs' loss to the New York Knicks in the 2026 NBA Finals has apparently kept star Victor Wembanyama up at night during the offseason.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Spurs' loss to the New York Knicks in the 2026 NBA Finals has apparently kept star Victor Wembanyama up at night during the offseason.

During NBA Media Day on Monday, Wembanyama revealed it's been "hard to fall asleep sometimes" after his team came up short in the Finals.

San Antonio took a big step forward in 2025-26, making a run through the Western Conference while taking down the Oklahoma City Thunder. However, Wembanyama and Co. could not finish the job when they went up against New York.

While the Spurs held double-digit leads in every game, they managed only one victory as the Knicks won the title in five games. Four of the five games were decided by four points or less.

Wembanyama had a strong statistical series, averaging 26 points, 11.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 3.6 blocks per game. However, his efforts weren't enough.

The 2025-26 Defensive Player of the Year averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds, 3.1 assists and a league-best 3.1 blocks per game during the regular season while shooting 51.2 percent from the field and 34.9 percent from deep.

He is the centerpiece of nearly everything the team does on both sides of the floor with his ability to protect the rim and clean the glass on defense and work in pick-and-pops, hit from the outside and attack the basket on offense.

There is maybe no bigger matchup nightmare in the league than Wembanyama. With the star saying he now has a new form of motivation, he could become an even bigger issue for the rest of the league.

articles.title: Alberto Díaz se rompió frente al Real Madrid: casi dos meses de baja
articles.standfirst: El base malagueño sufre una rotura muscular en el isquiotibial de su pierna izquierda y agrava los problemas de lesiones del Unicaja
articles.summary: El base malagueño sufre una rotura muscular en el isquiotibial de su pierna izquierda y agrava los problemas de lesiones del Unicaja
articles.body: Malas noticias para Alberto Díaz y para el Unicaja. El capitán del conjunto malagueño estará previsiblemente entre seis y ocho semanas de baja después de sufrir una lesión muscular en el isquiotibial de su pierna izquierda durante el estreno liguero ante el Real Madrid. El base malagueño tuvo que pedir el cambio en el tercer cuarto después de sentir un fuerte dolor en la pierna. «Me he roto», se pudo leer en sus labios mientras abandonaba la pista. Una sensación que posteriormente confirmó Txus Vidorreta en sala de prensa: «Lo primero que saco del partido es la lesión de Alberto, porque nos ha quitado mucho en defensa». A su regreso a Málaga, el capitán fue sometido esta mañana a pruebas médicas en el Hospital Quirónsalud Málaga que determinaron que sufre una lesión muscular en el isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda. El tiempo definitivo de baja dependerá de su evolución, aunque la primera estimación apunta a un periodo de entre seis y ocho semanas. El contratiempo llega en un momento complicado para el Unicaja, que ya cuenta con Kalinoski, Nzosa y Tyson Pérez en la enfermería. Además, Matt Thomas ha llegado con un contrato temporal para reforzar el perímetro y el club trabaja en la incorporación de un jugador interior. La lesión de Alberto Díaz deja a Vidorreta con solo dos bases disponibles: Kendrick Perry y Pantzar. Un problema añadido para un equipo que acaba de comenzar la temporada y que pierde a uno de sus principales referentes defensivos durante varias semanas.
