articles.title: Kristaps Porzingis Out Indefinitely, Jimmy Butler Injury Update Announced by Warriors
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are already battling the injury bug before the 2026-27 season begins.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are already battling the injury bug before the 2026-27 season begins.

Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. told reporters on Monday that veteran center Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to start training camp due to a health issue. Dunleavy added , "I'm not marking him down as being out to start the season or anything like that. He's just not available this week."

Dunleavy also provided an update on star forward Jimmy Butler III's recovery from a torn ACL, saying that he and injured guard Moses Moody have progressed to "very light on-court activities."

The Warriors are set to open training camp in Hawai'i before playing their first preseason game against the Los Angeles Clippers in Honolulu on Oct. 4. ESPN's Anthony Slater noted that Porzingis will not travel with the team, ruling him out for at least the first four practices and the preseason opener.

Golden State acquired Porzingis from the Atlanta Hawks at last season's trade deadline, but he appeared in just 15 regular-season games with his new team due to his recurring health issue. The 31-year-old has missed a combined 90 games over the last two regular seasons. Despite his injury history, the Warriors re-signed him to a two-year, $40 million contract this summer.

Slater reported that there was "internal optimism about how Porzingis looked this summer," as he appeared to be cleared for training camp before Dunleavy was informed about his latest health issue.

"He's been participating in everything," Dunleavy said. "It just kind of popped up."

Dunleavy expressed confidence that this latest setback won't hurt Porzingis' chances of being ready for the upcoming campaign.

"We feel comfortable with everything [about Porzingis' status]," Dunleavy said. "Disappointed that he won't be out there [when training camp starts Tuesday], but it's early, so don't want to overreact to anything."

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey Talks LeBron Relationship, Says Seeing Jaylen Brown in 76ers Uniform Is 'Awkward'
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Tyrese Maxey is still adjusting to life with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in Sixers uniforms.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Tyrese Maxey is still adjusting to life with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in Sixers uniforms.

During the team's media day, Maxey detailed how his rapport with James goes back years. The two became regular workout partners in the offseason. Still, it's a little "weird" to now be on the same side as the surefire Hall of Famer:

Maxey offered similar remarks about Brown, who went from being an on-court rival to a critical piece in Philly's hopes of reaching the NBA Finals:

Players have the flexibility to stage informal practice sessions with their peers during the summer. In terms of the preseason, though, there isn't much time for a reshuffled roster to build familiarity before opening night.

Training camps open Tuesday and the first preseason games get underway on Saturday. On Oct. 20, the Sixers have their first matchup of the regular season.

There's plenty of mutual respect between Maxey, James and Brown, and they've crossed paths on the court before. Still, nothing will prepare them for sharing the court together like the games themselves, so there's bound to be an adjustment period.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Says Jaylen Brown-76ers Trade Was 'Tough,' Talks Paul George's Impact with Celtics
articles.summary: When Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics take the floor this season, they will be doing so without former star Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
When Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics take the floor this season, they will be doing so without former star Jaylen Brown.

Tatum understands, though, that sometimes that's just the nature of the NBA.

While speaking to reporters at NBA Media Day on Monday, Tatum acknowledged it was "tough" seeing Brown get traded but noted he was "grateful" for what they accomplished together, which included an NBA championship.

Although Tatum will no longer be teammates with Brown, he will now get to play alongside Paul George, who came to Boston in the trade. Tatum revealed on Monday that he has "tried to steal things" from George's game.

It will be a new-look Boston squad after an eventful offseason.

Also of note, this will mark Tatum's first full season since he suffered a ruptured Achilles during Boston's 2025 playoff run. He recovered in time to make 16 regular-season appearances to close out the team's 2025-26 campaign.

On Monday, Tatum let it be known that he feels "great" and has gotten stronger during the offseason.

Tatum's health, as well as George's, will be very crucial to the Celtics' outlook this season.

If Tatum is able to play in 70-plus games and play up to his previous All-Star form, the Celtics could be in the mix in the East. However, with some changes to the roster, it could take some time for everything to come together.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Won't Answer Question About Who Is 'Alpha' on 76ers After Trade, LeBron Signing
articles.summary: After being traded from the Boston Celtics to the Philadelphia 76ers, star guard Jaylen Brown is joining a loaded lineup that also includes stars LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.
articles.body:
After being traded from the Boston Celtics to the Philadelphia 76ers, star guard Jaylen Brown is joining a loaded lineup that also includes stars LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

However, Brown isn't interested in discussing his new team's hierarchy. When asked during Monday's media day about who the " alpha " of the Sixers is, Brown told reporters, "Next question."

Of course, being the "alpha" of a team was a large part of the debate about the sustainability of Brown's role alongside Celtics star forward Jayson Tatum. Boston opted to break up its star tandem, despite the fact that it will now be facing Brown in division rivalry games.

While Brown isn't looking to discuss the Sixers' pecking order, it's fair to wonder about how the offense will flow with so many All-Star-caliber players.

For now, it sounds like Brown is willing to contribute however he's needed as the Sixers chase an NBA championship this year.

articles.title: Nikola Jokic Addresses Contract, Future amid Trade Rumors Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: Nikola Jokić's future with the Denver Nuggets will hover over the team until there is a long-term contract in place seeing how the 2026-27 campaign is the final one until his 2027-28 player option, but co-general manager Ben Tenzer believes the team is in a fine position.
articles.body:
Nikola Jokić's future with the Denver Nuggets will hover over the team until there is a long-term contract in place seeing how the 2026-27 campaign is the final one until his 2027-28 player option, but co-general manager Ben Tenzer believes the team is in a fine position.

"We feel very comfortable with the relationship, the trust there," he told reporters Monday. "We have no concerns."

Tenzer's belief seems to be warranted given Jokić's comments:

This comes after Kevin O'Connor of Yahoo Sports reported Saturday that "no really expects Jokić to leave Denver. Waiting also makes financial sense: Next summer, he could sign a projected five-year, $360 million deal—the richest deal in NBA history."

O'Connor also noted the future Hall of Famer told reporters in Serbian in July, "My idea and desire is to stay in Denver. I'll probably sign next year."

Jokić has been with the Nuggets his entire NBA career since they selected him in the second round of the 2014 draft. He is a franchise icon and one of the best players in league history and showed no signs of slowing last season while averaging 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds, 10.7 assists and 1.4 steals per game.

His resume includes a championship, an NBA Finals MVP, three league MVPs, eight All-NBA selections and eight All-Star nods.

At this point, there are no indications there will be any trade requests or drama when it comes to Jokić's future. Instead, both the player and front office seem to be on the same page, which will likely result in a massive deal next offseason.

Still, it will remain a focus until that deal is in place.

articles.title: La pesadilla de Antetokounmpo en Miami con las iguanas: "Si siguen apareciendo, me mudo"
articles.standfirst: El griego, fichaje estrella de los Heat, sufre al ver como su casa de 13,5 millones ha sido invadida por esos reptiles
articles.summary: El griego, fichaje estrella de los Heat, sufre al ver como su casa de 13,5 millones ha sido invadida por esos reptiles
articles.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo ya conoce a su primer enemigo en Miami. Y no mide 2,10, no juega en la NBA y tampoco defiende. Tiene escamas, cuatro patas y la mala costumbre de aparecer en su jardín. El nuevo fichaje de los Heat ha descubierto que su aterrizaje en Florida incluye un inesperado desafío: las iguanas. "Si las iguanas siguen apareciendo, probablemente me mude, quizá consiga un apartamento. Sin piscinas, sin césped, nada de eso", soltó entre risas durante el Media Day. La amenaza ha llegado demasiado pronto. Giannis se encontró el pasado viernes con una iguana en el jardín de su nueva casa de Pinecrest y el episodio acabó incluso con la intervención de un exterminador. Lo curioso es que el griego se ha gastado unos 13,5 millones de dólares en su nueva mansión, una espectacular propiedad de unos 12.000 pies cuadrados con piscina y jardín. Justo el escenario perfecto para sus nuevos vecinos. "Cuando llegué aquí en julio, alguien me dijo que eran bastante lindas. No son lindas. No son lindas. Dan miedo. Pero espero acostumbrarme. Ya veremos". Entre bromas y reptiles, Antetokounmpo empieza a descubrir que su vida ha cambiado por completo. Después de toda una carrera en Milwaukee, donde fue campeón y construyó su leyenda, estrena ciudad, estadio, compañeros, vestuario y hasta dorsal: el 7 será su nuevo número. "Me siento bien. Sigo sintiéndome raro: muchas cosas nuevas, nuevos aficionados, nuevo estadio, nueva ciudad, nuevo centro deportivo. Pero estoy bien. Siento que estas dos semanas, al estar alrededor del equipo, me han ayudado a entrar en el ambiente. Esta cultura encaja con mi personalidad". Pero detrás de la sonrisa y de la guerra contra las iguanas hay una misión gigantesca. Miami ha apostado fuerte por Giannis para volver a mirar de frente al anillo y el griego no se esconde: "El objetivo es ganar un campeonato. Ese es el objetivo". Junto a Bam Adebayo y las nuevas piezas del proyecto, entre ellas Klay Thompson y Bobby Portis, el dos veces MVP afronta una nueva aventura con las expectativas por las nubes. Y hay algo que Giannis ya ha decidido que no piensa echar de menos de Milwaukee. El frío, probablemente no. La nieve, tampoco. Pero Miami tiene un problema que ni siquiera un campeón de la NBA parece dispuesto a soportar: el tráfico. "Eso sí que lo odio", reconoció. De momento, el griego se adapta a todo: a una nueva ciudad, a una nueva camiseta y a una nueva vida. Sólo las iguanas parecen estar en condiciones de hacerle plantearse un traspaso.

articles.title: LeBron Explains Why He Snubbed Knicks for 76ers After Leaving Lakers in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: The New York Knicks' championship triumph took them out of the running before the LeBron James sweepstakes fully kicked off.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks' championship triumph took them out of the running before the LeBron James sweepstakes fully kicked off.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN's Dave McMenamin . "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

The 22-time All-Star added that the NBA media "wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all" if he had joined forces with a team that just won a title.

James has always been very purposeful with his decisions on and off the court.

In terms of his NBA legacy, there probably isn't much more the 41-year-old can do. He's universally considered one of the greatest players ever, but he faces an unbridgeable gap on Michael Jordan, at least in the view of those who put MJ ahead of him.

That doesn't mean James has stopped thinking about his career in narrative terms.

Just ask Kevin Durant how much winning a title can be discredited when you join an established power. Fair or not, his critics will always judge him for signing with the Golden State Warriors after they won 73 games and were one victory away from a second straight championship.

KD's relationship with Warriors fans was a little fraught , too. Such was the bargain when he teamed up with three stars (Stephen Curry, Draymond Green and Klay Thompson) so closely identified with the organization's success.

For LeBron, it might've been something similar on the Knicks when Jalen Brunson is now a sainted figure in New York sports lore.

James was never going to sign with a rebuilding team with so little time left in his career. He can't put a franchise on his back in the same way he could a decade ago, and he can't operate mentally more than one season at a time.

The Sixers presented him with an ideal situation where the roster should be good enough to compete for a championship, but they're far enough away from being the finished product that LeBron should be able to dodge the ring-chasing allegations.

articles.title: El Real Madrid activa la ficha de Nick Smith y podía debutar ante el Efes
articles.standfirst: El escolta, llamado a ser referencia ofensiva de los blancos, no se ha estrenado hasta ahora por unas molestias físicas que ya ha superado
articles.summary: El escolta, llamado a ser referencia ofensiva de los blancos, no se ha estrenado hasta ahora por unas molestias físicas que ya ha superado
articles.body: Nick Smith Jr. por fin podrá debutar con el Real Madrid. El escolta de 22 años y 1,88 metros firmó con el conjunto blanco el pasado 15 de septiembre pero no ha sido dado de alta en la Euroliga hasta este lunes. Eso significa que podría tener sus primeros minutos este martes en la visita al Anadolu Efes (19.00 horas) o este jueves en el cierre de la primera doble jornada frente al Hapoel Tel Aviv en Sofía (18.00 horas). El último fichaje del Real Madrid ha estado cerca del equipo desde que llegó. Pese a que ya se sabía que no iba a jugar, viajó con el resto a Abu Dabi para estar presente en la SuperCup que se acabaría llevando el conjunto blanco con victorias sobre el Dubai Basketball y el Olympiacos. Smith Jr. tampoco pudo disputar el estreno de la Euroliga frente al conjunto dubaití y se perdió el debut en Liga Endesa este domingo ante el Unicaja. La razón de esta demora en poder ver al escolta estadounidense son unos problemas físicas que sufría. "Vino con molestias y había riesgo de que si le forzábamos podía caer en una lesión de gravedad. Estamos al final de ese proceso, le vamos a ir incorporando para que sea uno más. Ahora parece que el tema está superado y va a ir entrando en la dinámica del equipo”, ha contado Pedro Martínez. Smith es un escolta con gran capacidad anotadora, con facilidad para el uno contra uno y se puede fabricar sus propios tiros. Jugando la temporada pasada en los Lakers junto a LeBron James y Luka Doncic tuvo medias de 6,2 puntos con un 39,5% en triples promediando sólo 12,5 minutos en 30 partidos. Con los South Bay Lakers, el equipo vinculado en la G League, sus cifras fueron de 19,7 puntos con un 35,3% desde el arco. Las dificultades que ha tenido el Madrid para hacerse con un jugador de sus características y sus buenas condiciones han hecho que las expectativas se disparen a su alrededor. Habrá que comprobar su adaptación al baloncesto europeo. Su estreno como madridista está al caer.

articles.title: LeBron James: "Tuve visiones de jugar en los Knicks y terminar mi carrera allí"
articles.standfirst: La nueva estrella de los Sixers confiesa que ese era su sueño... hasta que los neoyorkinos ganaron el anillo
articles.summary: La nueva estrella de los Sixers confiesa que ese era su sueño... hasta que los neoyorkinos ganaron el anillo
articles.body: La gran revelación del Media Day de los Sixers no fue su fichaje por Philadelphia, sino el destino que LeBron James llegó a imaginar para el último tramo de su carrera. El cuatro veces campeón reconoció que, antes de decantarse por los Sixers, Cavaliers, Warriors, Heat o Timberwolves, tuvo en mente a los Knicks. "Tuve visiones de jugar en el Madison Square Garden y terminar mi carrera allí", confesó a ESPN. "Uno de los mejores lugares en los que he jugado". La posibilidad era real hasta que Nueva York conquistó el campeonato en junio y puso fin a 53 años de sequía. Ahí LeBron cambió de planes. "Creo que es el mejor estadio del mundo para un jugador de baloncesto. Pero después de que vencieron a San Antonio, pensé: 'No puedo'. No pude hacerlo". El propio James explicó que el rechazo que habría generado su llegada a los Knicks como campeón recién coronado terminó haciendo inviable una operación que, según sus palabras, había contemplado seriamente. El 'King' incluso tuvo un mensaje para los medios que, en su opinión, no le habrían perdonado ese movimiento: "Ustedes no me habrían dejado decir eso, para nada". Y quiso cerrar cualquier polémica con un reconocimiento al campeón: "Mucho respeto para los Knicks, obviamente. Un equipo increíble, jugadores increíbles". También destacó a Jalen Brunson, al que definió como alguien que le encanta y al que considera "increíble". Mientras tanto, LeBron afronta su nueva aventura en Philadelphia con la ambición intacta. En el Media Day dejó claro que no llega para conformarse con una segunda ronda: "No dejé a mi familia para perder en la segunda ronda, lo sé", dijo. Su relación con Tyrese Maxey y el deseo de ayudar a Joel Embiid a conquistar su primer anillo fueron factores importantes para elegir a los Sixers. Y, aunque su futuro más allá de Philadelphia sigue abierto, James resumió su filosofía actual: "Sólo vive el momento... ya veremos que pasa".

articles.title: All-Star Brandon Ingram has partially torn Achilles, will miss start of Clippers' season
articles.summary: Ingram was acquired in the trade that sent Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Clippers forward Brandon Ingram has a partially torn Achilles tendon and won't be able to play at the start of the season.

Interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden revealed the news to reporters at Clippers media day Monday. It's not clear how long Ingram will be sidelined, but Redden told reporters that the partial tear projects to need about six fewer months of rehab than a full tear would.

"He won't be ready for the start of the season, "Redden said, per Yahoo Sports' Jeff Eisenberg. "We'll reevaluate when we get there."

The Clippers acquired Ingram in the trade that sent Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors . The Clippers also received Gradey Dick , unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in the deal.

The trade was initially agreed upon in June, but put on hold as the NBA conducted a salary cap circumvention investigation of the Clippers regarding their dealings with Leonard. The two teams completed the trade on Sept. 14 after the conclusion of the league's investigation.

Redden told reporters that Ingram's partial Achilles tear was discovered prior to the trade when he underwent surgery on his heel in May. Both injuries were repaired in the same procedure.

Ingram, 29, is a two-time All-Star who made his second All-Star team with the Raptors last season. He averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.7 blocks while shooting 47.7% from the field and 38.2% from 3 last season.

He was present and walking at media day Monday with no apparent issue.

With Leonard gone, Ingram was projected as a focal point of the Clippers' offense alongside point guard Darius Garland .

The Clippers will instead start the season shorthanded as they embark on a new era in the aftermath of the NBA's investigation that resulted in punitive sanctions on the team , including the loss of five consecutive first-round draft picks from 2029-33.

The Clippers open their season at home against the Sacramento Kings on Oct. 21.

articles.title: LeBron James: NBA legend quashes retirement talk as he gets set for record-extending 24th season with Philadelphia 76ers
articles.summary: LeBron James begins his record-extending 24th season on the road against the reigning champion New York Knicks, who ended 53 years of heartbreak for ‌the five boroughs in June; the 41-year-old four-time MVP took a pay cut and must now convince Philly they can lift the ​trophy
articles.body:
James will begin his expected final chapter at his inaugural camp with the 76ers.

He made the NBA world wait a few weeks before announcing his decision over the summer to join to Philadelphia on a two-year $8m (£6m) contract with a player option for next season.

If James wins a title in Philadelphia, the 76ers would be the fourth franchise to become champions with him on the roster.

James won two championships in Miami, one in Cleveland and one with the Los Angeles Lakers.

"I'm not going to speak to the future right now; I'd be doing myself a disservice," James said at the Sixers' media day.

"I'm just living in the moment, especially knowing where I am in my career.

"Me trying to focus on what my future looks like, I wouldn't be giving myself grace. I'm more in the present now, understanding that I'm in year 24... I just like being in the moment, and we'll see what happens."

And if that Philly title happens, it would give Joel Embiid his first ring - which is part of James' motivation.

"I didn't leave my family (in Los Angeles) to lose in the second round," said James, who will turn 42 in December. "I know that for sure. Work needs to be done and I'm ready to get to work."

Much as James did for Cleveland when he ended a 56-year championship drought for the city by leading the Cavaliers to the title in 2016, he's in Philadelphia largely to help snap a championship drought for the Sixers that stretches to 1983.

The Sixers went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round by the eventual champion New York Knicks.

"Understand that the noise is going to be the noise," James said. "What happens outside of this building is going to consistently happen, and it's going to be doubled and triple and quadrupled down on you. It just comes with the territory. I understand it.

"I think the luxury of my game is, I can do everything. Literally, I can do everything."

James, Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and the other new star Sixers player, Jaylen Brown, were all on hand for media day ahead of the start of training camp and what figures to be the most anticipated season in Philly since Julius Erving's heyday.

"I hope that I can bring that experience, bring that knowledge, bring the blueprint to the guys that's trying to accomplish some things that they haven't done in their career," James said.

"I've seen everything that this league has to offer on the floor and off the floor, so I hope that every single day with my approach to the game, approach to the work, that it can translate to every single guy."

articles.title: Brandon Ingram's New Injury Diagnosed After Surgery, Latest on Clippers Star's Timeline to Return
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers will be without Brandon Ingram to start the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers will be without Brandon Ingram to start the 2026-27 season.

Clippers interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden told reporters Monday the team found a partially torn Achilles in Ingram's foot following heel surgery. While he will not be ready at the start of the new campaign, Los Angeles plans on reevaluating him at that time to determine when he could return.

This is quite a blow for the Western Conference team, as Ingram was part of the return when it traded Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors this offseason.

If the Clippers were going to surprise and compete for a playoff spot during the upcoming campaign, the Duke product figured to be a major part of it. After all, he made his first career All-Star Game last season with the Raptors and looked to be half of a one-two punch with Darius Garland that was tasked with leading the offense.

Ingram averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game last season while shooting 47.7 percent from the field and 38.2 percent from deep.

While he isn't someone who can completely replicate the loss of a future Hall of Famer like Leonard, he would have at least been a key part of the group effort. And now the Clippers will take the court for their Oct. 21 opener against the Sacramento Kings without him.

If nothing else, this will put more responsibility on the shoulders of rookie Keaton Wagler.

Wagler was the No. 5 overall pick of the 2026 NBA draft and will now be the Clippers' go-to option on the wing until Ingram is ready to return. The Illinois product is just 19 years old, but he is also the biggest reason for optimism in Los Angeles after the NBA stripped the team of five first-round picks as part of its punishment for the Leonard situation.

The rookie will now be firmly under the spotlight from the moment he steps on the floor and will look to help make up for the loss of both Leonard and Ingram.

articles.title: Anthony Davis Addresses Wizards Contract After NBA Rumors Linked Him to LeBron, Warriors Trade
articles.summary: The 2026-27 season could be the first and last time Anthony Davis takes the court for the Washington Wizards.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 season could be the first and last time Anthony Davis takes the court for the Washington Wizards.

After all, he did not play for the team last season after it acquired him from the Dallas Mavericks. What's more, he has a player option for the 2027-28 campaign, which means it came as no surprise he addressed his future Monday during media day.

Davis told reporters he will decide on his contract "when the season is over. I'm going to go through the season, and kind of do what I do at a high level, and then, when it's over, you know, sit down and have those key conversations again with the front office."

This comes after ESPN's Shams Charania reported in June the Golden State Warriors were exploring ways to add LeBron James and Davis to a team that already had Stephen Curry and Draymond Green, although that didn't happen with the big man staying put and the King joining the Philadelphia 76ers.

While Washington hasn't made the playoffs since 2021, it selected AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick of the draft and added veterans like Khris Middleton and Deandre Ayton around Davis and Trae Young.

Notably, David Aldridge of The Athletic reported Monday both Davis and the Wizards agreed to delay any contract talks until after the start of the season so he can "assess whether Washington is a place where he wants to remain.

"Davis said, after he was acquired from the Mavericks in February, that he needed to see what steps the Wizards made to become a more competitive team this season, and what their plans were to make the team into a true contender in the next couple of years."

Washington could eventually offer the future Hall of Famer a four-year, $275 million max extension that ran through the 2030-31 campaign when he turned 38 years old, but Aldridge reported that is "highly unlikely" since he has a history of injuries and is older than some of the team's core group.

The Wizards also committed significant money to Young with a four-year, $212.8 million deal, so that would be quite a lot tied up in two veterans.

For now, though, Davis and the Wizards will focus on challenging for the playoffs during the upcoming campaign.

The 10-time All-Star's ability to stay healthy will go a long way toward determining whether that is possible, but the pieces are in place for Washington to at least be a threat in the conference.

articles.title: Lakers' Luka Doncic Drops Quote on NBA Championship Goal After LeBron James' Free Agency Exit
articles.summary: Despite losing star forward LeBron James to free agency, Los Angeles Lakers star guard Luka Doncic isn't backing down from his lofty expectations.
articles.body:
Despite losing star forward LeBron James to free agency, Los Angeles Lakers star guard Luka Doncic isn't backing down from his lofty expectations.

While speaking to reporters during Monday's media day, Doncic declared that winning an NBA championship is a realistic goal for the Lakers this season.

"If that's not your goal, I don't know what you're doing here," he told reporters .

Doncic's partnership with James came to an end this summer when the 41-year-old opted to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. Doncic said Monday that he's ready to step up as a leader for a new-look Lakers team that will be integrating multiple new faces this season.

"It feels great. Obviously, it's a new challenge," Doncic told reporters . "I was in this position in my career a lot of times, so it's not new to me. But I feel great, I feel excited, and like I said, I'm ready to go."

While the Lakers didn't make many splashy moves this offseason, Doncic told reporters that he feels new Laker additions are "underrated." One of the team's top acquisitions was rising star center Walker Kessler, and Doncic made it clear that he and management were aligned with the move, telling reporters , "I really wanted him."

Doncic was in the midst of an incredible 2025-26 campaign before he suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in April. In 64 games, he led the league with 33.5 points per game while also averaging 7.7 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.6 steals. The 27-year-old told reporters that he's fully recovered from his hamstring injury and expects to be playing with no restrictions during the upcoming campaign.

Doncic and the revamped Lakers will open the preseason on Oct. 5 against the Sacramento Kings.

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Jokes He'll 'Dropkick' Anyone Who 'Pisses Me Off' During NBA Games After Trip to China
articles.summary: Dillon Brooks is known as one of the NBA's so-called villains, and he had some fun with that reputation Monday during media days.
articles.body:
Dillon Brooks is known as one of the NBA's so-called villains, and he had some fun with that reputation Monday during media days.

The Phoenix Suns swingman told reporters , "if anyone pisses me off, giving them dropkicks—especially the ones in stripes," when asked how his training he learned in China will help him this season.

He was joking and then clarified that he actually believes he will have a better mental approach because of the trip.

Phoenix would surely welcome that, as Brooks led the league with 17 technical fouls last season.

He never hesitates to talk trash or take a physical approach to defense, even when he is matched up with some of the league's biggest stars such as LeBron James. That approach, along with the technical fouls, has created his reputation.

However, a different mental approach could help him become even more effective in 2026-27 as he looks to help the Suns reach the playoffs as an important role player alongside Devin Booker and Jalen Green.

articles.title: Luka Dončić says it 'feels great' to be the leader of the Lakers following LeBron James' exit
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is ready to be the Lakers' leader.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is used to being the alpha on his team. Dončić filled that role with the Dallas Mavericks , where he became the team's de-facto star and leader on and off the court.

A surprising trade to the Los Angeles Lakers in 2025 upended all of that. With LeBron James in town, Dončić had to adapt to a new role. He may have still been the best player on his team, but James was the captain of the ship.

With James now a member of the Philadelphia 76ers , Dončić said it "feels great" to assume his old role and take over as the Lakers' leader.

Dončić's comment was probably not meant to be a dig at James, as the two seemingly got along very well with the Lakers. It was likely more a comment on Dončić feeling comfortable as a team leader, a role he filled for years with the Mavericks.

Dončić explained as much while giving his answer. "I was in this position in my career a lot of times, so it's not new to me," Dončić said. "I feel great. I feel excited."

The shift from James to Dončić started before the offseason. With James out with an injury early last season, Dončić put the team on his back, averaging 34.4 points per game over his first 10 games.

That seemed to set the tone for the season, as Dončić's average barely went down even when James returned. Dončić averaged 33.3 points the rest of the way, firmly putting himself in the MVP discussion until a late injury knocked him out of the running to win the award.

With James now gone, the Lakers are officially building around Dončić. This offseason, that meant trading for Walker Kessler and re-signing Austin Reaves . Dončić spoke extremely highly of both players when asked about them Monday.

Now that the team has a new look, the Lakers are looking for a better result in the playoffs. After losing to the Oklahoma City Thunder last season, Dončić said the team's goal is a championship. "If that's not your goal ," Dončić said Monday. "I don't know what you're doing here."

articles.title: Ben Simmons Wants to 'Dominate' With Kings, Opens Up About Hiatus in New Video After NBA Return
articles.summary: Ben Simmons isn't exactly setting the bar low for his return to the NBA after taking the 2025-26 campaign off.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons isn't exactly setting the bar low for his return to the NBA after taking the 2025-26 campaign off.

"To dominate," he told reporters Monday when asked what his personal goals are with the Sacramento Kings (6:10 mark). "Every time I step on the floor to dominate."

Simmons joined the Kings on a one-year, $3.5 million deal this offseason after he did not play in the NBA at all last season. He believes that time away will help him return to form.

"I'm right where I need to be," he said (15-second mark). "I took a lot of time to focus on my body over the season. I think it's the best thing I've done and decision I've made for my career."

Notably, he also said (4:15 mark), "I'm there," when asked if he could return to his peak. "He's there. He woke up."

Kings fans will surely love to hear that, as there was a time when Simmons was one of the best players in the league who could impact games in a number of ways.

The No. 1 pick of the 2016 NBA draft was the Rookie of the Year and a three-time All-Star during his first four seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers. He was also an All-NBA Third Team selection in 2019-20 in the first of back-to-back seasons when he was named to the All-Defensive First Team.

However, he missed the 2021-22 campaign with injury and was never the same player.

Simmons appeared in 42 games in 2022-23, 15 games in 2023-24 and 51 games in 2024-25 and never averaged better than 6.9 points per game in that span. A hesitancy to shoot or attack the basket made him a liability at times on the offensive side, which limited his overall value even as a solid defender who can rebound and facilitate.

ESPN's Marc J. Spears reported Simmons "impressed" Kings head coach Doug Christie, general manager Scott Perry and other members of the team during workouts this offseason, though, which inspired the team to sign him as someone who can play all five positions and back up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr.

Simmons won't be a focal point of the team like he was in Philadelphia, which should take some of the pressure off his shoulders and could help him thrive in a new role.

articles.title: Curry renuncia a millones para que los Warriors vuelvan a volar
articles.standfirst: La estrella de Golden State 'perdona' 20 millones al no querer firmar por el contrato máximo para dejar un mayor margen salarial a la franquicia y poder aspirar al anillo
articles.summary: La estrella de Golden State 'perdona' 20 millones al no querer firmar por el contrato máximo para dejar un mayor margen salarial a la franquicia y poder aspirar al anillo
articles.body: La decisión de Stephen Curry de continuar en los Warriors va mucho más allá de una renovación al uso. El líder de los Golden State aceptó cobrar por debajo del máximo al que podía aspirar para facilitar que la franquicia tenga mayor margen de maniobra salarial y pueda reforzar una plantilla que pretende volver a competir por todo. Curry, que encara su decimoctava temporada en la NBA, firmó finalmente una extensión de dos años y 116 millones de dólares, frente a los aproximadamente 136,7 millones que podía haber percibido de haber elegido el máximo. La diferencia ronda los 20 millones. No se trata, por tanto, de una simple cuestión económica. Es un movimiento con un claro componente deportivo y sentimental. "Este es mi hogar. Esto es lo que hemos construido. Esta es una comunidad ante la que he jugado durante toda mi carrera y poder terminar esta historia de la manera correcta es una parte importante de ello", afirmó Curry en el Media Day. El cuatro veces campeón de la NBA deja así claro que su futuro está ligado al único equipo en el que ha jugado en la liga y que quiere escribir los últimos capítulos de su carrera en San Francisco. El nuevo contrato le llevaría, si ejecuta su opción de jugador, hasta 2028-29, lo que supondría alcanzar las 20 temporadas con los Warriors. El sacrificio tiene además una finalidad concreta: ganar. "Se trata de que, para que tengamos una oportunidad esta temporada, que empieza mañana, de jugar al baloncesto y competir, todos tenemos que hacer nuestro trabajo para ganar. Todos lo sabemos, yo incluido. Tengo que estar sano y disponible", explicó. Y añadió: "Después vas alcanzando distintos hitos a lo largo del año, lo que nos permite conservar la mayor flexibilidad posible, sin saber exactamente lo que eso puede significar. Sí, me ofrecieron el máximo. Sí, todas las opciones estaban sobre la mesa, y probablemente todo lo que hayan escuchado sea, de alguna manera, cierto". Los medios de la Bahía han destacado que esa estructura puede proporcionar a Golden State alrededor de 10 millones adicionales de margen salarial el próximo verano. Curry no quiso esconder que detrás de los números hay una apuesta por el proyecto. "Para mí, se trataba simplemente de procesar todo eso para llegar a la decisión que fuera adecuada para mí y para el equipo. Creo que todos somos gente inteligente en esta sala, así que pueden leer entre líneas por qué el contrato está estructurado de esa manera". Es el mensaje de una estrella que, a los 38 años, ha decidido poner parte de su fortuna al servicio de la última gran oportunidad de los Warriors. Después de 17 años, cuatro anillos y más triples que nadie en la historia de la NBA, Curry no sólo ha elegido dónde terminar: también ha aceptado ganar menos para intentar que Golden State tenga más recursos para rodearle.

articles.title: Everything Bronny James Said About LeBron Leaving Lakers for 76ers in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Bronny James will play in the NBA on a different team than his famous father for the first time in his career during the 2026-27 season, and the Los Angeles Lakers guard is looking forward to seeing how things unfold.
articles.body:
Bronny James will play in the NBA on a different team than his famous father for the first time in his career during the 2026-27 season, and the Los Angeles Lakers guard is looking forward to seeing how things unfold.

"It's something different for sure," he told reporters Monday when discussing not playing with LeBron James. "I'm excited for the experience, to experience something different with him not being here and to see how the staff treats me without him being there and all my teammates and stuff like that. I'm excited for it, and I'm excited for the season."

He expanded on those comments as media day continued:

He will get to spend Christmas Day with his father, though, as the Lakers will host the Philadelphia 76ers.

The younger James averaged just 4.8 points per game during his one collegiate season with USC, so it wasn't difficult to speculate the King's presence on the Lakers played a role in the team's decision to draft his son in the second round in 2024.

Bronny James was also just a secondary role player for the Purple and Gold during his first two seasons, but he showed signs of taking a leap.

He increased his points (2.3 to 2.9), assists (0.8 to 1.2) and steals per game (0.3 to 0.5) from his first to second season. He also improved his overall efficiency as his field-goal percentage jumped from 31.3 to 40.9 and three-point percentage jumped from 28.1 to 38.6.

What's more, he scored five points and saw important time during Game 3 and Game 4 of Los Angeles' first-round playoff victory over the Houston Rockets.

"I'm coming in like I'm playing against the Houston Rockets last year in the playoffs," James said Monday. "I'm coming in aggressive, I'm coming in playing smart, playing my game, and whatever the team needs I'm that guy."

That should help him continue on the upward trajectory fans saw from his first to second seasons even if he is no longer teammates with his father.

articles.title: Ja Morant Open to Blazers Bench Role, Emphasizes Desire to Win After Trade from Grizzlies
articles.summary: Ja Morant indicated on Monday that he would be open to a bench role with the Portland Trail Blazers if that's what the team felt was necessary.
articles.body:
Ja Morant indicated on Monday that he would be open to a bench role with the Portland Trail Blazers if that's what the team felt was necessary.

"I think winning is the most important thing for me," he told reporters when asked about his potential role and if being a starter was important to him. "So whatever role I have to play to get that done, I don't think anybody would be mad after a win. As a starter, if I'm starting, if I'm not, it's the same thing. It's day one right now, I feel like that's coach's questions, but for me I have no problem with either."

articles.title: Aday Mara se mira en el espejo de los Gasol: "Pau y Marc tuvieron un gran impacto en mi crecimiento"
articles.standfirst: El pívot de los Thunder quiere recoger el testigo del enorme legado que dejaron los hermanos de Sant Boi en la NBA
articles.summary: El pívot de los Thunder quiere recoger el testigo del enorme legado que dejaron los hermanos de Sant Boi en la NBA
articles.body: Aday Mara aterriza en la NBA con una generación de gigantes españoles sobre sus hombros. El pívot zaragozano, elegido con el número 12 del último Draft por los Oklahoma City Thunder, no olvida a quienes abrieron el camino antes que él. "Mi generación está agradecida a los de antes: los hermanos Gasol, Ricky Rubio, Navarro, Llull, todos esos jugadores. Esa generación fue grande. Ver sus partidos y cómo luchaban por ser los mejores fue muy importante. Los hermanos Gasol tuvieron un gran impacto en mi crecimiento, aunque siempre digo que tomo muchas cosas de muchos jugadores", explicó en el Media Day de Oklahoma. Y entre todos ellos hay dos nombres que ocupan un lugar especial. Pau y Marc Gasol fueron mucho más que dos compatriotas triunfando en la NBA para el joven Mara: fueron sus referentes desde niño. En Estados Unidos, el propio pívot ha contado que veía muchos vídeos de los dos y que intentaba incorporar elementos del juego de ambos. "Obviamente, Marc Gasol, Pau Gasol. Eran grandes. Pero también veía a Arvydas Sabonis, Olajuwon", recordó. La influencia no se queda en la admiración. Mara ha explicado que su intención siempre ha sido aprender de diferentes leyendas y construir su propio juego a partir de ellas: "Con esto no quiero decir que me parezca más a un jugador que a otro. Sólo significa que intento coger una cosa de Olajuwon, otra de Pau y otra de Marc". Una filosofía que encaja con su perfil de pívot pasador, con recursos en el poste y capacidad para proteger el aro, características que durante años identificaron también a los dos hermanos. El vínculo con aquella generación española tiene además una dimensión emocional. Mara ha reconocido que los Gasol fueron parte de su crecimiento mientras veía a la selección y a los grandes jugadores españoles competir al máximo nivel. "Nuestra generación en España es muy afortunada porque tuvimos delante a la generación de oro y a los hermanos Gasol", aseguró en otra entrevista. Ahora le corresponde a él prolongar una tradición de pívots españoles que pasó de Pau a Marc y que tiene en Mara a uno de sus nuevos protagonistas. El salto al vestuario de Oklahoma supone, precisamente, empezar a escribir su propia historia. "La primera impresión que tuve fue que era muy distinto con respecto al 'college'; esto es otro nivel. Estar alrededor de jugadores como Chet [Holmgren] y de veteranos impacta, pero luego se te pasa. Al final vas a jugar al baloncesto, aunque el primer impacto es, sin duda, importante", reconoció. Mara llega a los Thunder después de conquistar la NCAA con Michigan y lo hace llevando consigo algo más que una mochila de expectativas: también la inspiración de aquellos Gasol que, cuando él era niño, demostraron que un pívot español podía conquistar la NBA.

articles.body: Welcome to NBA Media Day, where 28 teams around the league are set to hold interviews and press conferences leading up to training camp practices.The Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks aren't included in today's groups, after holding their respective media days last week leading up to their preseason games in Macao, China.That still leaves plenty of interesting storylines for the rest of the league, however. Fans will get their first look at LeBron James as a Philadelphia 76er following a blockbuster offseason signing in free agency, while we also get to hear directly from Kawhi Leonard amid the fallout of the NBA’s investigation into salary cap circumvention allegations with the LA Clippers. Follow along with Yahoo Sports as we highlight the biggest news and storylines from 2026-27 NBA Media Day.

articles.title: Doncic se pone la corona de los Lakers: "Estoy listo"
articles.standfirst: El esloveno acepta el desafío de tomar en solitario el mando del equipo angelino tras haber compartido el trono con LeBron James
articles.summary: El esloveno acepta el desafío de tomar en solitario el mando del equipo angelino tras haber compartido el trono con LeBron James
articles.body: La corona ya ha cambiado de dueño en Los Ángeles. En su primer Media Day como líder absoluto de los Lakers tras la marcha de LeBron James, el esloveno Luka Doncic asumió sin rodeos el desafío de encabezar una franquicia que exige volver a pelear por todo. "No diría que es distinto (ser la estrella de los Lakers). Sin duda ha habido grandes nombres, pero es un nuevo desafío. Me gusta. No digo que sea distinto, pero me siento honrado", afirmó el esloveno. Doncic no se esconde ante la responsabilidad. Ser el rostro de los Lakers, después de ocho años de LeBron en el centro de la escena, supone un salto enorme, pero él lo afronta desde la confianza de quien ya ha cargado con el peso de una franquicia. "Es un nuevo desafío. He estado en esta posición muchas veces en mi carrera, no es algo nuevo. Estoy listo para afrontarlo", sentenció. Y si había alguna duda sobre cuál es el objetivo en el nuevo ciclo, Doncic la despejó de golpe: el anillo. "Realmente, diría que el campeonato. Si ese no es tu objetivo, no sé qué estás haciendo aquí. Me gustaría que todos viniéramos para aprender algo nuevo cada día. A nivel individual, obviamente, me gustaría ganar el MVP algún día, pero eso no llegará si no somos buenos como equipo", explicó. La ambición individual queda, por tanto, supeditada al éxito colectivo. Doncic llega además después de un verano de descanso que le ha permitido recuperar fuerzas y afrontar por primera vez una temporada en Los Ángeles sin compartir jerarquía con LeBron. "Me siento bien, descansé y, a nivel mental, me siento genial", aseguró. La prensa de Los Ángeles viene destacando precisamente ese cambio de liderazgo: Los Angeles Times ya habla de que "se ha pasado la corona" y sitúa a Doncic como el eje sobre el que los Lakers han construido su nuevo proyecto. La transformación también ha sido reconocida desde dentro. Rob Pelinka, prsidente de Operaciones y General Manager de los Lakers, ha definido a Doncic como "el mejor jugador ofensivo del mundo" y ha explicado que la reconstrucción del verano se diseñó específicamente para rodearle de las piezas necesarias. Además, antes del Media Day, el propio Doncic había resumido su evolución en un aspecto clave: "Hace cinco años estaba en mi tercer año en la Liga. No era el líder que se suponía que debía ser, así que creo que el liderazgo es una parte importante de mi situación ahora."
